God of my mercy and my praise
God of my mercy and my praise,
The sinners speak against thy grace
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 109:1–5, 31, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1O God of my praise, be not silent. 2For wicked and deceitful mouths open against me; they speak against me with lying tongues. 3They surround me with hateful words and attack me without cause. 4In return for my love they accuse me, but I am a man of prayer. 5They repay me evil for good, and hatred for my love. 31For He stands at the right hand of the needy one, to save him from the condemners of his soul. PSALM 109:1–5, 31 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 109
Their malice rag'd without a cause, Yet, with his dying breath, He pray'd for murderers on his cross, And blest his foes in death. STANZA IV
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 109. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
